scope: Worktree /home/user/holyagent-identity (node_modules installed; mise available). Diff without dist and .holyagent: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/e4ac10e5-b710-572b-aa70-34045c8c8d11/scratchpad/identity.diff.

Intent: in claude.ai (CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true) commits use the account owner as author (author.name/author.email in local git config, set by the new vcs identity command from the GitHub connector) and keep the cloud committer Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>, so the Anthropic signature verifies; outside claude.ai behavior is unchanged; identity guidance appears in session context only in the cloud; nothing identity-related is written to repository files.

result:
result: No blockers. All 8 `/code-review` findings are non-blocking or rejected. `mise run verify` passes (808 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail), but the tree was not mutated, so "fails without the change" is judged by reading. Evidence is from a settled tree (`git status` clean).

changed: none (read-only). `/code-review high 4702068...a5575f1` ran through the Skill tool and loaded the built-in review.

checks:
- `mise run verify` in `/home/user/holyagent-identity` -> exit 0. Type-check: no errors in 103 files. Lint: no problems in 104 files. Format: 217 files formatted. Tests: 808 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail, 5437 expects.
- Manual git probes in temp repos: `git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT` honours `GIT_AUTHOR_*` over `author.*` over `user.*`. Git is 2.43.
- Not run: a real claude.ai commit signature check, and the GitHub connector's `get_me`. Whether Anthropic's signature verifies with a user author and a Claude committer is read from the intent, not run.

blockers: none

notes (each classified from the `/code-review` claims):

Non-blocking
1. `packages/runtime/src/vcs/commit.ts:90`, `requireOwnIdentity` checks only `user.*`, not the author git would use. Outside a cloud session a commit can pass the check yet be authored by an agent.
   - Scenario: `user.*` is a person and `author.*` or `GIT_AUTHOR_*` is Claude.
   - This is the same as the base, so it is not a regression. The new `vcs identity` command makes `author.*` a documented key, so the gap is more reachable. The non-cloud test 'the author setting is ignored' pins this behavior.
2. `packages/runtime/src/vcs/errors.ts` (CloudAuthor hint) and `commit.ts:44`: with `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME` or `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL` set to an agent in the environment, the environment wins over `author.*`, which I probed.
   - Scenario: `vcs identity` succeeds, `vcs commit` still refuses with CloudAuthor, and the hint says to run `vcs identity` again, which loops. The hint never mentions the environment variables.
   - This is the precedence behavior the cloud tests cover with a refusal, so it is correct but not self-healing. The hint could name them.
3. `packages/runtime/src/vcs/author.ts:30-37`: `--name ','` or `';'` passes validation. I probed git, and `git var` then fails with "name consists only of disallowed characters", so `vcs commit` reports "(none set)" and the hint loops back to `vcs identity`.
   - The `/code-review` example `'.'` is rejected: git accepts `. <a@b.c>`.
   - A GitHub name made only of punctuation is implausible.
4. `packages/runtime/src/vcs/identity.ts:3`: `/^claude\b/i` rejects a real user named "Claude Dupont" (also `looksLikeAgent`'s original rule on the base). `vcs identity` and CloudAuthor now apply it to `get_me` names. The hint offers only the login when the name is empty, so such a user has no path. This is a limited false positive and the rule already existed for `user.name`.
5. `packages/runtime/src/cli/hook.ts:210-214`: a cloud session whose main thread is already the holyagent agent, in a project with no `.holyagent` and no legacy folder, gets no author text. The test 'says nothing to a root with neither' asserts this on purpose. The first `vcs commit` then refuses with the CloudAuthor hint, which carries the full steps, so the session recovers. This matches the intent only partly ("guidance appears in the cloud").
6. `packages/runtime/src/vcs/author.ts:38-39`: the two `git config` writes are not atomic. A failure between them leaves `author.name` set with `author.email` at `user.email` (noreply@anthropic.com). The next `vcs commit` refuses, so the state is detected and the command can simply be re-run.
7. `packages/runtime/src/vcs/commit.ts:44`: when no identity is configured, `git var GIT_AUTHOR_IDENT` can return an auto-detected `user@host`, which passes. In claude.ai `~/.gitconfig` always sets `user.*` to Claude, so this does not occur in the target environment.
8. `packages/runtime/src/state/tree.ts:201` repeats the ident regex that `parseIdent` provides (`parseIdent` forbids angle brackets in the email). `tree.ts` is untouched by this change, so this is optional dedup.
9. Rejected: two identity checks selected by `cloud` (`requireOwnAuthor` and `requireOwnIdentity`) is a design preference. The split is justified because the non-cloud path must stay unchanged.

Scope and compatibility:
- Nothing identity-related goes into repository files. `identity` uses `git config --local`, which lives in `.git/config`. A test asserts `git status` and `ls-files` are unchanged.
- The cloud switch is the strict `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE === "true"`. `"false"` and `"1"` are tested as non-cloud.
- Docs, `dist` and requirements text changes are consistent with the code.
- The generated `dist` is not covered by a rebuild check here (not examined beyond the plugin tests, which pass).

Test judgment (read, not run against the base):
- `vcs identity` writes only the two keys, validation refusals write nothing, and the missing or agent-like author is refused with exit 3. All of these fail on the base: the command does not exist, and the base would refuse the cloud commit with AgentIdentity.
- The cloud test 'the author is the user and the committer stays Claude' asserts the `%an|%cn` pair on a real commit. It fails on the base. The `GIT_AUTHOR_*`, `author.*` and environment-variable cases are covered.
- The non-cloud test passes on the base too. It is a regression guard, not a change test, which is acceptable.
- The hook and session-context tests assert the text is present only when `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true`, its position, and the context budget. The plugin test asserts the static root prompt has no identity guidance. All of these fail without the change.
- Gap: no test covers the `--name ','` case (note 3) or a `GIT_AUTHOR_*` environment variable overriding a good `author.*` (note 2).
